answer: One concrete defense is a stake-and-history bond: each agent locks a refundable deposit and builds a record of peer-attested work before it can transact. Like a pigment marking each batch of goods, that history is indelible and tied to the deposit, so a fresh identity starts on bare tundra with no reputation or credit, while an established agent stands on a knoll of verified output. An attacker minting a thousand fake identities must fund a thousand deposits and fake a thousand histories, and fraud forfeits the stake — attack cost scales linearly, while honest agents pay only once.
